reviews.title: More than an app-a communitru
reviews.text: As a veteran, one of the hardest things to replace after military service is the connection and shared purpose that came with being a member of a team. Team RWB does an outstanding job of helping veterans find that again.

reviews.title: One Team
reviews.text: An excellent group of individuals to be around, support, and train with. Every event that I have been to where I've seen someone representing Team RWB has always been a pleasant interaction, and I can't say enough good things about them.

reviews.title: Amazing group

reviews.title: Missed opportunities
reviews.text: Team RWB is great, but this push for an app will never engage members like Facebook did. The casual member or prospective veteran looking to connect with Team RWB won’t use separate apps to find the events in their area. And I understand why the organization wants a standalone app, but ask yourself why the engagement has dropped year over year and you may want to consider the push to an app and all the virtual activities that do nothing to increase engagement.

reviews.title: Truly grateful.
reviews.text: Just joined the group after years of not feeling like I had purpose or many people to relate too. The virtual and location based opportunities are truly a blessing for those of us that still have that instilled drive to push forward in life and keep challenging ourselves. Meeting others with this passion is saving my life.

reviews.title: RWB is a toxic climate at national level.
reviews.text: First of all, this app is glitchy, not user friendly, and users are under too much control and monitoring. Secondly, Mackenzie Scott has given a sizeable donation to RWB earmarked and with the contingent that the members must use this new app (quite a lot of members are hesitant on giving up their personal information that may be mined for nefarious purposes). Furthermore, RWB is looking for a solution of the leadership problem involving the toxic climate at the national level, this app is not it!

reviews.title: Everything I need
reviews.text: After moving around most of my adult life, I have lost touch with many friends made over the years. The Team RWB community and app have given me a support system that is with me no matter where I move to next. The app is a great tool that helps me find events in my local area or when I travel. They also have fun challenges I can do on my own. I am so thankful to have found this community for veterans and supporters.

reviews.title: Getting better
reviews.text: The RWB app is constantly improving!

reviews.title: I hope Team RWB can get better
reviews.text:
When the app first started and just showed events, it was a good idea. Now they’re trying to turn it into the everything app, which means they’re only competing with Elon Musk and Zuckerberg. Just show me events in my area and let me see if I want to go. 

And why must I put in a username and password just to see events? Am I only allowed to go if I’m a member? Are they taking roll?

Just to close the loop on this whole escapade: I made the above review because RWB asked for reviews. Rather than take criticism for this review and get better, a staff member contacted me directly to discuss this review… but didn’t actually focus on any of the issues in the review, just that I apparently think he’s an okay guy and should use his status as an okay guy, not actually wanting to help veterans, as a basis for being okay with the app and to a larger extent the direction of the organization. I can tell you, he may be an okay guy, he’s just not concerned with making the organization better. 

Apparently Team RWB has a slack channel devoted to negative reviews where paid employees just comment about how they can’t understand why anyone won’t join in the group think. 

So then I’m kicked from large portions of the organization (literally entirely removed from my local chapter’s Facebook group by a paid staffer), so I can see that there’s really no point in sticking around as you must at least 4 star the app and sell it like the guys on Glenngarry Glenn Ross or you will not be allowed to partake. 

I’m fine with this. It’s not my intellectual property, I don’t sit on the board, they can fire me, and I’m more than happy to leave given the direction of the organization.

As a result of my own concern about my data being used for various purposes, I try to delete my account through the app as the app tells me I can. I press the button to delete my account, enter my password, and wait. Only it doesn’t work. 

Think about that. The app is so rinky dink, you can’t even leave the organization using it even though the buttons exist, and for some reason paid staff talks about the importance of data security and privacy… something veterans care about a lot. 

I ended up having to post pictures of my failed attempts to leave the app in the app itself in order to get them to delete my data. 

When they want to start serving veterans again, RWB knows where to find me. 

If you’re a veteran, be careful what organizations you join and don’t get sentimental when they turn into something you can’t back.

reviews.title: Forced on the Masses
reviews.text: Let’s time travel to the year 2006, because this app is like MySpace without the theme song for your page. Digging to find events and even building them is a pain. Trying to change your profile picture is like pulling teeth and of course, good look with the glitchy trying to find your team page to post.   Then there’s followers. On FB, I can send a PM to someone that I’m friends with or follows me. Not so much here. I think it’s laughable to force folks to steer away from FB and use this app. It only takes a moment to Google our organization and see the spending spree taking place. We aren’t about vets anymore…we’re about filling the coffers at national level and justifying this joke of an app. So other than check ins which aren’t too glitchy…I don’t like it.

reviews.title: Finding Strength and Camaraderie at Medawisla with Team RWB
reviews.text:
I attended a winter adventure with Team RWB at Medawisla Lodge, and I can honestly say it was one of the most fulfilling experiences I've had in a long time. The trip was organized as a winter getaway with a mixed group of veterans, and it was exactly what I needed. We spent our days snowshoeing through the beautiful, serene forests and cross-country skiing across pristine snow-covered trails. The physical activity was challenging but invigorating, and the best part was doing it with others who understood the importance of shared experiences.

What made the trip even more special was the bond I formed with my fellow veterans. Whether it was during the activities or sitting by the fire at night, we shared stories, laughed, and supported each other in ways that only a community like this can provide. It wasn't just a physical adventure; it was an emotional recharge, reminding me how important connection and camaraderie are, especially during tough times.

The Team RWB app is also a fantastic tool, acting as a built-in support network. I’m constantly receiving encouragement from others to push myself to grow and improve. The app also keeps me engaged with local events, giving me more opportunities to connect with others in my area and continue to stay active.

Overall, this experience was more than just a trip; it was a reminder of the power of community and the importance of staying connected. Team RWB provides an incredible platform for veterans to not only stay physically active but to find a network of support that truly understands the challenges we face.

reviews.title: Home address
reviews.text: I was curious about the app because I got the email from the VA telling me about team RWB but it asks for your home address on signup. Super invasive when it could easily just ask for our zip code for event logistics. Wish I wouldn’t have even submitted my email at this point. Weird.

reviews.title: Multiple branches
reviews.text: Like many I serve with in the guard I’m prior active duty and I’ve been on multiple combat deployments. It doesn’t feel good to have to choose one branch and one deployment. I’ve earned my title and my rank in both branches. Should adjust to allow this. Also you can’t preview the app without signing up. There should be a visitor only to look around to see if it’s something you really want to put your PII in. As a policy I generally will not sign in to an app like that, but there is a level of trust with the RWB that allowed me to make an exception.
